Your boat is 12 meters long (anchor in the bow) the water depth is 7 meters, the anchor cable is 70 meters long and there is a strong side wind blowing from starboard of the bow. Where will you cast the anchor?
answer_text: I will cast the anchor perpendicular to the tie point, as far as possible from the dock.
note: Drop the anchor at right angles to the quay and as far out as the rode allows.

question: You are sailing on motor, on course 180°. The real wind is from the north, the wind gauge is indicating 12 knots, your boat speed is 12 knots, what is the real wind in the area?
answer_text: 24 knots.
note: Apparent wind vector maths, including the following-wind case, is taught.

question: What information can you find in the “PILOT BOOK”?
answer_text: Most of the information you need for navigating and routing in the given area.
note: Pilot books and what they contain are taught.

question: You are sailing on course 150°, the wind is south west at 5 on the Beaufort scale, one of the shrouds that was under load has torn. What will be your reaction?
answer_text: The shroud is on the starboard side so you must execute a turn to reduce the pressure on the mast.
note: On course 150 with a south-west wind the starboard shroud is loaded; the course says turn to put the broken side to leeward.

question: Which is the most accurate statement?
answer_text: In a close reach, the speed is a little better than in a beam reach, there is lee way, the sails aretaught close to the keel line and there is healing.
note: Left out on purpose: the official answer looks wrong (close reach is not usually faster than a beam reach).

question: In the “CADINAL” buoy system you see a yellow and black buoy, and above it the following sign             in black. On which side of the buoy should you pass?
answer_text: One must pass the buoy to the east.
note: Cardinal top marks and colors are taught; the pictured mark is judged from the answer.

question: What will the prop work of a right hand propeller cause, with the engine engaged in reverse and the steering neutral?
answer_text: Veering of the bow to port.
note: Left out on purpose: the official answer (bow to port in reverse) contradicts the course and another exam answer.

question: What is the approximate direction of the real wind when the wind gauge on your boat is showing a south wind, and you are sailing west?
answer_text: South east.
note: The course teaches that apparent wind shifts forward of the true wind when moving.

question: What is the role of the tie ropes called “SPRING” ropes?
answer_text: These are ropes that prevent boat movement along and in parallel to the dock (after the boat is tied).
note: Springs run diagonally and stop the boat moving along the dock.

question: While sailing your boat (engine + sails) the propeller has come off, what must you do?
answer_text: I must lower the cone, the boat will be considered a sailboat in terms of rules of the sea.
note: The course teaches the motor-sailing cone and that a yacht not using its engine is a sailing vessel.

question: You are sailing in torrential rain in a 23 meter boat, and can hardly see the bow of your boat, which is under sails only. What audible signal will you sound?
answer_text: One long blast followed by two short blasts at intervals of no more than 2 minutes.
note: The fog signal for a sailing vessel (one prolonged, two short, at most 2 min) is taught.

question: The wind is directly from the east (at 9 knots) and you are sailing under sails on a course of 125° and having difficulty maintaining the sailing course. What might be the possible reason for that?
answer_text: You are too close to the wind, your speed in the water is too low.
note: Pinching too close to the wind and losing speed is taught.

question: What is a “BOOM – VANG” (BOOM- JACK) used for in a system of sails.
answer_text: To secure the boom so it does not rise in broad winds.
note: The vang stops the boom rising on a reach or run.

question: You are sailing in good visibility in a narrow sea channel and hear behind you two long blasts and one short blast. What is the meaning of the signal?
answer_text: A motorized vessel is about to pass you on the starboard side.
note: Two prolonged and one short means overtaking on the starboard side, now taught.

question: Which is the most correct statement?
answer_text: A “bora” is: a catabatic strong and dry north east wind in winter, occurring in the Adriatic Sea.
note: Lesson describes the Bora as a cold, dry, gusty north-easterly falling from mountains in the Adriatic winter.

question: Which is the most accurate statement?
answer_text: In the zone between a warm front and a cold front, the isobars are almost straight lines.
note: Lesson says isobars are almost straight in the warm sector.

question: In the attached barometric chart, what is the wind direction at point B?
answer_text: None of the above answers is correct.
note: The answer depends on the exam's attached weather chart, which is not available; the course does give the general rules.

question: Which of the following items is not found in a life raft? (as part of the permanent equipment)
answer_text: A portable S.A.R.T. device.
note: A SART is a separate grab-bag item, not raft equipment.

question: What are, usually, the requirements of a tow rope?
answer_text: That it has high tensile characteristics.
note: A tow line needs a high breaking strength, as taught.

question: How is the weight of the anchor determined relative to the size of the vessel?
answer_text: In the safety equipment regulations of the Israel Ports Authority there is a reference to this question.
note: Israeli note says anchor weight is set in the Ports Authority safety equipment regulations.

question: In the sailing log it is customary to list the following data: a- Odometer         b- engine temperature c- distress signals         d- wind direction          e- cloud cover f- vessel location g- oil pressure h- wind speed i- names of crew on shift Of the above, which ones can help you determine the vessel’s course?
answer_text: a, h, d, f.
note: The log records distance run, wind speed and direction, and position, for dead reckoning.

question: which of the vessels listed below fulfills the definition of a “fishing vessel engaged in fishing”?
answer_text: All the above answers are correct.
note: The course defines engaged in fishing as gear that restricts maneuvering, and includes trawling.

question: In a single engine boat with a single shaft and right hand propeller. What will be the effect of engaging the engine in forward gear?
answer_text: The bow of the boat will veer sharply to port.
note: Going ahead, prop walk is weaker and the other way: stern to starboard, bow to port.

question: In the attached barometric chart, choose the most accurate statement regarding the visibility.
answer_text: At point A the visibility is very limited.
note: The answer depends on the exam's attached weather chart, which is not available; the course does give the general rules.

question: With respect to the attached barometric chart, when sailing from Cyprus to Israel (on a course of 150 º) on what tack will the boat be sailing? (during most of the trip)
answer_text: Beam reach on a port tack.
note: The answer depends on the exam's attached weather chart, which is not available; the course does give the general rules.

question: Based on the attached chart, what will affect the island of Cyprus?
answer_text: The cold zone of the winter low.
note: The answer depends on the exam's attached weather chart, which is not available; the course does give the general rules.

question: Which is the most accurate statement of the following options regarding the “breeze” in our area?
answer_text: The “breeze” typical of our area in the summer, is caused by the temperature difference between the sea and the land.
note: Lesson says the sea breeze comes from the land-sea temperature difference.

question: G is a motorized vessel and sees vessel K sounding the audible signal depicted in picture 119. What is he signaling?
answer_text: K is in distress and needs assistance.
note: A continuous horn is taught as a distress signal.

question: What is a vessel displaying the signal depicted in picture 81 signaling?
answer_text: A grounded vessel.
note: Three black balls mean aground, as taught.

question: Sailboat O notices vessel C displaying the lights depicted in picture 53. What is the vessel and what is the required action? (there is apparent risk of collision).
answer_text: C is a vessel towing and must yield. Sailboat O will continue on its course.
note: An ordinary tug and tow keeps clear of a sailing vessel, as taught.

question: A vessel displaying the signal depicted in picture 84 is sailing at a distance of about 100 meters from shore (declared bathing beach). What do the regulations stipulate about it?
answer_text: It is breaking the law. It is not allowed to sail in a declared beach area.
note: Israeli note forbids sailing in a declared bathing beach, fishing vessels included.

question: What day signal will the vessel displaying the lights depicted in picture 53 display?
answer_text: There is no need for a day signal.
note: A tow under 200 m shows no day shape, as taught.

question: What day signal will a vessel display that is displaying lights as depicted in picture 39?
answer_text: The signal depicted in picture 81.
note: Aground day signal of three black balls is taught.

question: Vessel M is a sailboat running, the main sail is on the starboard side. It notices vessel E displaying the lights depicted in picture 37 (the light intensity is growing). Indicate the correct answer.
answer_text: M is a gaining and passing vessel, so there is no significance to the tack. M will yield way.
note: Seeing only a sternlight means overtaking, which keeps clear regardless of tack.

question: What is a vessel displaying the flag depicted in picture 92 and above it a black ball signaling?
answer_text: I am in distress and need assistance.
note: A square flag with a ball above it is taught as distress.

question: You notice a white light in front of your boat’s bow, what might it be and what will be your action? (the light intensity is increasing)
answer_text: This is the stern light of a vessel. I will yield to it.
note: A lone white light may be a sternlight and the overtaking vessel keeps clear.

question: While sailing a sailboat, you notice in front of your boat’s bow a vessel displaying the lights as depicted in picture 39. What is the vessel signaling and what will be your action?
answer_text: That it is grounded so I must be careful.
note: Aground lights and the warning to keep clear are taught.

question: You are on vessel H on a course of 340ºdisplaying the lights depicted in picture 1. You are in danger of collision with P, displaying the lights depicted in picture 58. The wind is west. What will be youraction?
answer_text: Turn about 50 degrees to starboard.
note: Both are sailing vessels head-on; with a west wind H is on port tack and gives way with a large early turn.

question: You are on boat J under sails only, on a starboard tack, and see vessel B displaying the shape depicted in picture 80. What is the required action?
answer_text: J yields to B in the most effective way.
note: Two black balls mean not under command; a sailing vessel keeps clear.

question: Vessel J on sailing course 020 º and displaying the lights depicted in picture 1, is in danger of collision with B, displaying the lights depicted in picture 58. The wind is from the west. What is the required action? (north is to the top of the page)
answer_text: J yields in the most effective manner.
note: With a west wind J on 020 is on port tack and B on starboard tack, so J gives way.

question: Vessel J displaying the day signals depicted in picture 84 sees vessel D displaying the flag depicted in picture 98 on the mast and a black ball in the bow. What is the vessel signaling and what is the required action?
answer_text: It is an anchored vessel with divers so one must keep at least 200 meters distance.
note: Flag A plus an anchor ball means anchored with divers; keep 200 m off.

question: Sailboat (H) notices motor boat (L) sounding the signal depicted in picture 119. What is the requiredaction?
answer_text: L is in distress, H must go offer assistance.
note: A continuous horn means distress, and the duty to help is taught.

question: Dual engine vessel (O) notices motor boat (B). What is the required action?
answer_text: B yields to O.
note: The power-driven crossing rule is taught; number of engines does not matter.

question: A vessel displaying the lights depicted in picture 55, what day signal must it display?
answer_text: As depicted in picture 84.
note: Picture 55 is red over white (fishing); its day shape is two cones points together (picture 84).

question: Sailboat “K” on a port tack in a north wind, sees sailboat “A” with the mainsail on its port side. What is the required action?
answer_text: “K” yields since it is on a port tack.
note: Port tack keeps clear of starboard tack, judged by the mainsail side.

question: Sailboat (F) notices sailboat (C), the wind is from the south. What is the required action?
answer_text: F yields to C, F is on the windward side on the same tack.
note: Windward boat on the same tack keeps clear.

question: Motor boat (A) notices row boat (D). what is the required action.
answer_text: A yields to D, a motorized yields to a row boat.
note: Israeli note says motorboats give way to rowing boats.

question: Sailboat “O” displaying the day signal depicted in picture 82, sees “M” displaying the day signal depicted in picture 84, and in addition the day signal depicted in picture 85 on the port side. What is the requiredaction?
answer_text: “O” is motorized and “M” is a fishing vessel, the obligation to yield is with “O” so it must keep its distance from the hazard on the port side.
note: Cone point down makes O power-driven; two cones mean fishing and the cone point up marks gear out on that side.

question: Vessel “M” displaying the lights depicted in picture 43, sees “E” displaying the same lights. There is danger of collision. What is the required action?
answer_text: M yields to E.
note: The power-driven crossing rule is taught (see the flag on this answer in the report).

question: Vessel “C” displaying the day signal depicted in picture 84, sees “G” displaying the day signal depicted in picture 81. What is the required action?
answer_text: “C” is a fishing vessel, “G” is grounded, you must keep as far away as possible.
note: Fishing cones and the aground three balls are taught.

question: Vessel J sailing on course 022° and displaying the lights as depicted in picture 1, is in danger of collision with vessel B displaying the lights depicted in picture 66. The wind is west. What is the required action?
answer_text: B continues on course and speed as much as possible.
note: Picture 66 is not under command seen head-on; the sailing yacht keeps clear and B stands on.

question: Vessel K displaying the lights depicted in picture 16, sees vessel C displaying the lights depicted in picture 28. What is the required action?
answer_text: Each turns to starboard.
note: Hovercraft and tug meet head-on; both turn to starboard.

question: Vessel K displaying the lights depicted in picture 14, sees vessel G displaying the lights depicted in picture 55. What is the required action? (the wind is north)
answer_text: K yields to G.
note: K is a sailing vessel over 20 m and G is fishing (red over white); a sailing vessel keeps clear of fishing.

question: Vessel G displaying the signal depicted in picture 82 sees vessel O displaying flag 98 over the structure and a black ball in the bow area. What is the required action?
answer_text: One must keep at least 200 meters distance from vessel O, it is anchored and engaged in diving.
note: Flag A plus an anchor ball means anchored with divers; keep 200 m off.

question: Motorized vessel (K) displaying the day signal depicted in picture 86 notices sailboat (C) on a port tack. What is the required action?
answer_text: K yields to C.
note: A diamond marks only a long tow, an ordinary power vessel that gives way to sail.

question: Sailboat (M) displaying the day signal depicted in picture 82, notices row boat (D), and there is danger of collision. What is the required action?
answer_text: M yields to D.
note: Israeli note says sailing boats also give way to rowing boats.

question: You are sailing sailboat A, the wind is north, your boat speed is 12 knots, you notice sailboat I its speed is 8 knots. Sailboat A is on a starboard tack and sailboat I is on a port tack. What is the required action?
answer_text: Based on the rules of the sea A must yield to I.
note: Overtaking overriding the tack rule is taught.

question: You are sailing in a sailboat and see in front of you what is depicted in picture 39. How should you act?
answer_text: It is a grounded vessel over 50 meters in length, I will move away from the danger.
note: Anchor lights for 50 m+ plus two reds mean a large vessel aground, as taught.

question: Vessel “M” displaying the day signal depicted in picture 86 is in danger of collision with vessel “K” displaying the same day signal. What is the vessel and what is the required action?
answer_text: M is towing with a line over 200 meters. M yields.
note: Diamond means a tow over 200 m; the ordinary crossing rule decides who gives way.

question: A north wind while sailing on sails due east and you notice on your bow a vessel, displaying the lights depicted in picture 58. How will you act?
answer_text: A sailboat on a starboard tack so I must yield to it.
note: Sailing east in a north wind you are on port tack; the head-on sailing vessel is on starboard tack, so you give way.

question: A vessel displaying the lights depicted in picture 38, what day signal will it display?
answer_text: As depicted in picture 75.
note: Picture 38 is three reds, constrained by her draught, whose day shape is a cylinder (picture 75).

question: Vessel “K” displaying the lights depicted in picture 11, sees vessel “O” displaying the lights depicted in picture 14. What is the required action?
answer_text: Based on the regulations, O yields to K.
note: K is a tug restricted by her tow (red-white-red); a sailing vessel keeps clear.

question: You are on a vessel departing the Herzliya marina at night, what lights do you expect to see on the breaker in relation to your boat’s bow?
answer_text: Picture 74.
note: Leaving an Israeli harbor the lights are reversed: green on your left, red on your right.

question: What lights will a vessel flying flag 95 during the day turn on at night? (in a marina)
answer_text: As depicted in picture 13.
note: A vessel carrying dangerous goods shows an all-round red light at night (flag B by day).

question: Sailboat (O) notices vessel (M) also a sailboat, the wind is south. What is the required action?
answer_text: M is windward of O, and yields to it.
note: Windward boat on the same tack keeps clear.

question: When might a boat encounter the danger of an uncontrolled gybe?
answer_text: When running.
note: The risk of an accidental gybe near dead downwind is taught.

question: You are sailing a sailboat on course 300°. The wind is from the north at 10 knots. You would like to change course to 060°. How will you do so most effectively?
answer_text: I will turn the rudder to starboard and perform a turn.
note: Turning the bow through the wind (tack) and helm direction are taught.

question: You are sailing a 12 meter long boat due north west. Besides you there are five crew members on board for whom this is their first sailing, amongst them 3 children. The wind is south west (240º ) at 15 knots with gusts to 20 knots. You are sailing with a full array and your boat assumes a sharp lean every time there is a wind gust. You would like to improve the situation. What should you do?
answer_text: I will reduce sails and consider sailing on foresail alone.
note: Reducing sail when overpowered and heeling hard is taught.

question: The boat is moving backwards. You would like to turn the bow to starboard. In which direction should you turn the wheel?
answer_text: To port.
note: The course teaches steering works the opposite way going backward.

question: You notice a vessel during the day flying flag A. What does this flag indicate, how will you react, and what lights will this vessel display at night?
answer_text: A divers flag, I will keep 200 meters away. At night the vessel will display the following lights: red, white, red surround.
note: Flag A, red-white-red at night and the 200 m distance are all taught.

question: To what distance from shore can a vessel go that is on a sailing trip within the coastal waters.
answer_text: Up to 12 miles from shore.
note: Israeli note says a coastal (national) voyage may go up to 12 NM from shore.

question: What are the boundaries of a beach marked as a declared bathing beach restricted to vessels?
answer_text: 50 meters on each side of the declared area, and 300 meters to sea from the low tide line.
note: Israeli note gives the 50 m and 300 m bathing beach limits.

question: You are approaching a marina and you notice a vessel standing in the entrance and flying flag B of the international signal codes. How will you act?
answer_text: I can enter the marina, but avoid getting too close to the ship as a precaution.
note: Flag B near a harbour entrance: enter but keep clear, as taught.

question: When will you use a parachute flare?
answer_text: Both at day and night.
note: Parachute rockets are for day or night.

question: You are sailing a sailboat at night. In front of your bow you see lights, as depicted in picture 36. What is the required action?
answer_text: I will maintain course and speed.
note: Picture 36 is a large power-driven ship head-on, which gives way to sail, so you keep course and speed.

question: At night you notice a vessel displaying the navigation lights as well as a white surround light, and above it a green surround light. What is the day signal this vessel should display?
answer_text: Two triangles with their tips joined together.
note: Trawling lights green over white and the two-cones day shape are taught.

question: In the “CARDINAL” buoy system you notice nine short flashes within 15 seconds. On which side should you pass the buoy?
answer_text: West.
note: Nine quick flashes mean a West cardinal mark: pass west.

question: Select the correct statement:
answer_text: A foam extinguisher is appropriate for a liquids fire.
note: Foam is mainly for burning liquids.

question: When does one anchor with two anchors?
answer_text: All the above answers are correct.
note: Two anchors: one cannot hold, wind and current differ, or a reversing river current.

question: In what position will the foresail be in a “HEAVE TO”?
answer_text: When it is taut to windward.
note: Hove to, the headsail is held tight on the windward side.

question: The visibility is good and a vessel on your starboard sounds seven short horn blasts that mean:
answer_text: Your intentions are unclear.
note: At least five short rapid blasts for doubt about intentions is taught.
